paper_sections.title: Comparison of Hemodynamic Brain Responses Between Big Wave Surfers and Non-big Wave Surfers During Affective Image Presentation

description.value: The study compared hemodynamic brain responses and task-related functional connectivity between big wave surfers and non-big wave surfers during presentation of affective images differing in valence and arousal.

spans.text: We conducted 2 (group: BWS vs. CON) by 2 (arousal: high vs. low) by 2 (valence: negative vs. positive) ANOVA model to examine the main effects of group, arousal, and valence as well as the interaction effect.

design.value: An event-related fMRI study in which 23 surfers viewed randomized positive and negative IAPS images with high and low arousal, including fixation trials, followed by group-level ANOVA, post-hoc group comparisons, and generalized psychophysiological interaction analyses.

spans.text: We used an event-related design with jittered inter-stimulus interval in current study.
Thus, the behavioral task consisted of 180 trials, lasting 7.5 min.

We conducted 2 (group: BWS vs. CON) by 2 (arousal: high vs. low) by 2 (valence: negative vs. positive) ANOVA model to examine the main effects of group, arousal, and valence as well as the interaction effect.

Behavior Task Participants viewed a series of images from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS) while undergoing brain fMRI.

task_description.value: Participants viewed 160 affective IAPS images categorized by valence and arousal, plus 20 fixation trials, in randomized order.

spans.text: IAPS images were categorized according to valence (positive or negative) and arousal ratings (high or low), creating four groups: high arousal positive (HAP), high arousal negative (HAN), low arousal positive (LAP), and low arousal negative (LAN).
An additional 20 trials were included in which no image was presented, and participants continued to view the fixation cross (FIX trials).
